content.title: Oscars 2026: One Battle After Another wins best picture | CBC
content.text: March 16And that's a wrapMichael B. Jordan poses with the Oscar for best actor for Sinners at the Governors Ball following the 98th Academy Awards. (Carlos Barria/Reuters)This was definitely a difficult Oscars to predict, but for the most part, the chips fell to where they were projected. One Battle After Another was the ultimate champion and Sinners made some serious history — while Marty Supreme went home empty-handed.Here are some of the biggest moments of the night:OBAA snagged some of the night's top awards, including best picture. It also championed in adapted screenplay, casting, editing, supporting actor for Sean Penn and directing.Sinners won four statues off of a record 16 nominations: original screenplay, original score, best actor for Michael B. Jordan and cinematography. Autumn Durald Arkapaw is now the first woman, and first Black person, to win that last award.Canadians had a bit of a banner night, including the makeup and hairstyling and production design teams behind Frankenstein who helped the horror film pull in awards. There was James Cameron's Avatar: Fire and Ash, which won best visual effects, and also The Girl Who Cried Pearls, which won best animated short. Toronto's Maggie Kang saw her film KPop Demon Hunters win two trophies.The Singers and Two People Exchanging Saliva tied for best live-action short film, only the seventh tie in Oscars history.Mr. Nobody Against Putin staged a bit of an upset, toppling projected winner The Perfect Neighbor for best documentary feature.Host Conan O'Brien managed to sneak in some jokes at Hollywood's expense, as well as a few targeting Timothée Chalamet and U.S. President Donald Trump. Find our full list of winners here. One Battle After Another wins its last fight Jackson WeaverOne Battle After Another director Paul Thomas Anderson and cast members celebrate. (Mike Blake/Reuters)One Battle After Another managed to hold onto projections throughout the awards season that started to get somewhat more dicey as the Oscars crept up.The Paul Thomas Anderson-directed and -written film managed to capture six total wins tonight, off of 13 total nominations. While many Academy Awards forecasters had OBAA since it premiered in September, Sinners' momentum had many whispering of a potential surprise win. It was Anderson in the end, but Sinners was no slouch, pulling in wins in a host of contested categories. That technically still makes it the losingest film in Oscars' history; last year, Emilia Pérez tied Becket, Johnny Belinda, The Turning Point and The Color Purple in having lost 11 categories. This year, Sinners missed out on 12. Still, wins in best actor, original screenplay and original score did help cement it as a dominant performer; Sinners had the second-most trophies of the night. CHEERS for MBJ from the press roomEli GlasnerMichael B. Jordan wins the Oscar for best actor for Sinners. (Mike Blake/Reuters)I’ve been covering the Oscars for CBC News for over a decade and I have never seen the press room erupt the way it did when Michael B. Jordan won best actor for his role as Smoke AND Stack in Sinners. There were members of the press on their feet; the official academy librarians and IT support were standing up, applauding, hooting and hollering. As Jordan began his acceptance speech, saying “God is great,” it was like a church meeting, with the press responding at the screen with “that’s right” and “speak on it.” Jessie Buckley wins best actress for HamnetChristine PagulayanJessie Buckley of Hamnet wins the Oscar for best actress. (Kevin Winter/Getty Images)That's a sweep for Jessie Buckley and the first Oscar win for Hamnet. Buckley has now won all the major best actress awards for her performance as Agnes Shakespeare in Chloé Zhao's film. This is her first Oscar. In addition to the Academy Award, Buckley has won the Golden Globe, the Critics' Choice Award, the Actor Award and the BAFTA Film Award. She is the first Irish performer to win the category at the Oscars, BAFTAs and the Actor Awards.Last year's best actress winner Mikey Madison presented the award. "It's Mother's Day in the U.K. today," Buckley said in her acceptance speech. "I would like to dedicate this to the beautiful chaos of a mother's heart."Michael B. Jordan does the impossible Jackson WeaverMichael B. Jordan wins the Oscar for best actor for Sinners. (Patrick T. Fallon/AFP/Getty Images)There was an eruption of applause here in the little CBC meeting room. Michael B. Jordan did what seemed impossible only a few months ago, in winning best actor. Jordan's Sinners win was at the expense of Timothée Chalamet for Marty Supreme, the clear favourite for months. But a surprise BAFTA loss to Robert Aramayo, and then an incredibly surprising win for Jordan at the Actors swapped the betting odds in Jordan's favour. But the sheer fact that Jordan acted in a horror movie (which tend to perform poorly at the Oscars) and the fact he was in a more populist, popcorn-fare type movie than Chalamet made it seem hard to believe. But of course, all that doubt came to nothing.Paul Thomas Anderson breaks the best director curse Jackson WeaverPaul Thomas Anderson wins the Oscar for best director for One Battle After Another. (Mike Blake/Reuters)In a rather tense moment, the cards ended up falling the way we predicted. It's the fifth win for One Battle After Another tonight, and Paul Thomas Anderson's second gold of the night. It marks the beginning of the tough section of these awards — this trophy, and many of the categories coming up, are tightly contested. And in most of those categories, the challenger is Sinners. Ryan Coogler was a dark-horse candidate for this category, but Anderson instead took it home. "You make a guy work hard for one of these things," Anderson joked, referencing the fact that he's been up for (and lost) the category four times in his career.Golden takes the gold for original songMakda GhebreslassieEjae wins the Oscar for best original song for KPop Demon Hunters' Golden. (Kevin Winter/Getty Images)As many expected, Golden, the hit song from KPop Demon Hunters, won the Oscar for best original song. This also marks the second Oscar win for the film, which includes best animated feature. This is a history-making run for K-pop at the show."This award is not about success; it's about resilience," said EJAE, one of the song's writers and performers. She also squeezed in a shoutout to Canadian Maggie Kang, the movie's writer and co-director, before the rest of the team was played out. The realness of The Voice of Hind RajabMakda GhebreslassieThe Voice of Hind Rajab was one of five films nominated for best international feature film. It's a Tunisian film that tells the true story of Hind Rajab. The Palestinian girl and her family were in their vehicle when Israeli forces fired on them. The six-year-old was on the phone with dispatchers, begging to be rescued but help didn’t arrive in time. Canadian co-producer Odessa Rae told CBC the film’s director wanted to capture as much of the truth as possible while recreating what happened. The actors didn't rehearse with the actual recordings of Rajab. "She made this choice to feed the real audio of the little girl into their ear only after action was said." 1st overt mention of PalestineNick LoganPriyanka Chopra and Javier Bardem present the award for best international feature film. (Patrick T. Fallon/AFP/Getty Images)Ahead of announcing the international feature film nominees alongside Priyanka Chopra, presenter Javier Bardem said “no to war” and “free Palestine," in the first mention of the war since the show began. International feature film Oscar goes to Sentimental ValueNick LoganJoachim Trier accepts the award for best international feature film for Sentimental Value. (Patrick T. Fallon/AFP/Getty Images)Norway’s Sentimental Value won the Academy Award for best international feature film. The movie was nominated for nine Oscars tonight, including several acting awards and best picture. "All adults are responsible for all children," director Joachim Trier said in his acceptance speech.
